stem: Powers of Attorney must be signed by principal, dated, signed, and notarized.
why: The Uniform Power of Attorney Act took this away.

flashcard.front: Powers of Attorney must be signed by principal, dated, signed, and notarized. True/False
flashcard.back: False. The Uniform Power of Attorney Act took this away.

keyFact: POA must be signed, dated, and notarized: False, the UPOAA took this away

stem: Who can remove an agent from authority of a power of attorney?
why: A & D: the principal and a judge.

flashcard.front: Who can remove an agent from authority of a power of attorney?
flashcard.back: The principal and a judge (A & D)

keyFact: Who can remove a POA agent: principal and a judge

stem: If there are 3 or more agents appointed under the same power of attorney, they can act
options: Individually unless otherwise provided by POA
keyFact: 3+ agents on one POA: act individually unless the POA says otherwise

stem: Under the Uniform Power of Attorney Act, a power of attorney executed after Nov 1st, 2021 and absent any instruction of the document is presumed to be
keyFact: POA executed after Nov 1, 2021, no instruction: presumed durable

stem: Principal can execute a power of attorney even if they cannot physically provide a wet ink signature.
why: Someone can sign at their direction (incapacitated, blinking, etc.).

stem: Which is NOT a fiduciary duty of a trustee?
options: Manage the person's money and property carefully and separately from their own
Exercise care and good faith of the person's finances
Do not use the funds under any circumstances
why: It is not a fiduciary duty to not use funds under any circumstances.

stem: Which of these is an action that might be taken after the death of the grantor on a revocable living trust?
options: Visit with the funeral home without expenses
Amend the powers of the trustee
keyFact: After grantor's death, revocable living trust: obtain a TIN

stem: A trustee can always delegate routine tasks.
why: Trustees may delegate investment and management functions (60 O.S. §175.69), but that doesn't mean they can delegate routine tasks like signing checks or making deposits.

flashcard.front: A trustee can always delegate routine tasks. True/False
flashcard.back: False. Only when the trust (or power of attorney) says so.

keyFact: Trustee delegating routine tasks: only when the trust says so

stem: A grantor surrenders ownership, authority, and control over the trust and the trust property and income in which of the following?
why: In an irrevocable trust the grantor doesn't have authority, ownership, or control.
keyFact: Irrevocable trust: grantor gives up ownership, authority, and control

stem: A trust agreement establishes which of the following?
options: Limitations on the powers of the trustee
keyFact: Trust agreement establishes: trustee limits, revocability, successorship, delegation (all of the above)

stem: In a trust, the Grantor gives which party the right to hold title to property or assets for the benefit of a Beneficiary?
why: A Trust creates a fiduciary relationship: the Grantor/Trustor gives the Trustee the right to hold title for the benefit of a Beneficiary.
keyFact: Trust roles: Grantor/Trustor gives, Trustee holds title, Beneficiary benefits

stem: A trust established by a will, after the Grantor's death, is called a
keyFact: Trust created by a will after death: Testamentary Trust

stem: A trust established by a written document during the Grantor's lifetime is called
keyFact: Trust created during the Grantor's lifetime: Inter Vivos (Living) Trust

stem: The property conveyed into a Trust creates the trust
why: The trust corpus is sometimes called the principal, estate, or res.
keyFact: Property conveyed into a trust: the corpus (principal, estate, or res)

stem: If a Trust was created by a will, how are assets transferred into the Trust after the Grantor's death?
options: Through probate procedures in the court system
By the Trustee signing a transfer form at the bank
Automatically on the date of death
By written consent of the beneficiaries
keyFact: Testamentary trust assets: transferred in through probate

stem: When there are co-trustees, the law presumes that majority action is required unless the Trust instrument directs otherwise.
why: 60 O.S. §175.17: majority action is presumed unless the Trust instrument directs otherwise.
keyFact: Co-trustees: majority action presumed unless the trust says otherwise (60 O.S. §175.17)

stem: A dissenting co-trustee is not liable for the majority's action if they express their dissent in writing to the co-trustees at or before the time of the act.
keyFact: Dissenting co-trustee: not liable if dissent is in writing at or before the act

stem: Trustees may delegate investment and management functions.
why: Per 60 O.S. §175.69. That still doesn't let them delegate routine tasks like signing checks or making deposits.
keyFact: Trustees may delegate: investment and management functions (not routine tasks)

stem: A trustee may appoint an attorney in fact (other than a co-trustee) as the trustee's agent when
options: The Trust documents give the trustee that ability
The trustee is out of town
why: Pay close attention to the language in the Trust: the trustee must be given that ability in the Trust documents, unless the agent is another co-trustee.

stem: Which of these is NOT one of the documentation types for creating a trust?
why: The documentation types listed: Trust Agreement/Declaration of Trust, Last Will & Testament, Memo of Trust, and Certificate/Authorization Agreement.
